A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MotionEcho, with matching authors, core framework, and retained experiments despite the changed title. All 33 pages of v1 and 48 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TurboBench and AnimateBench experiments, component and hyperparameter ablations, qualitative results, and a 50-participant user study.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds DiT-based evaluations, LOVEU-TGVE results, sensitivity tests, motion-type analyses, memory measurements, and a failure case.

M1.justification: v2 adds DiT/flow-model adaptations using MOFT, DMT, and DiTFlow objectives, reference key/value injection, and iterative latent optimization (Section 3.5, Appendix A.1). Algorithm 1 also changes teacher re-noising from the student's motion-unguided prediction to its motion-guided prediction. Appendix C still uses the unguided estimate, leaving that particular procedural change internally ambiguous.

E1.justification: TurboBench and AnimateBench remain. v2 adds LOVEU-TGVE's broader appearance and motion editing scenarios, comprising 76 videos and 304 edit pairs, and easy/medium/hard prompt conditions on DavisBench (Section 4.1, Appendix B.4). This expands the tested editing conditions; DAVIS source data itself was already represented in v1.

E2.justification: The original TurboBench and AnimateBench comparator sets remain. v2 newly evaluates MOFT and DiTFlow on DiT systems, including direct distilled-model controls, and adds Tune-a-Video and PointMotion to the LOVEU-TGVE comparison (Tables 2, 7–8, 10–11). Tune-a-Video and the work called PointMotion were previously cited but not evaluated as these comparators.

E3.justification: v2 adds DiT model configurations and Flow-sim, Appearance Diversity, and Pick Score evaluations. Reported TurboV2 settings also change: activation thresholds move from 380–420 to 480–500, truncation becomes motion-dependent, and noise blending changes from k=0.01 to 0.05 or 0.3. The motion-strength sweep changes from 500–2000 to 0.05–0.2. These are reported setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 expands guidance-strength sweeps and adds activation/truncation sensitivity tests, motion-type and optical-flow analyses, direct VB-only controls, memory/time analysis, and a climbing-motion failure case (Tables 4–5, 9–10, 12; Figure 8). Conversely, v1's separate inverted-noise component ablation and both noise-blend-factor sweeps are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The 50-participant, 36-pair user study retains the same reporting practice and percentages.

E6.justification: TurboBench scores, AnimateBench scores, and user-study percentages are retained. v2 adds extensive DiT, LOVEU-TGVE, subgroup, sensitivity, and resource results. For example, its new Table 10 reports VB+DiTFlow at MF 0.540 and 34 seconds versus MotionEcho at 0.733 and 54 seconds. These are newly reported comparisons, not v1-to-v2 performance gains. Noise-initialization ablation results are removed.

T1.justification: The endpoint interpolation already appears in v1 Equation 5. v2 corrects the squared-loss gradient step factor from lambda to lambda/2 and adds derivations of its proximal formulation and equivalent noise-prediction correction (Appendix C). These provide a limited formal extension of the existing update.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that direct motion guidance struggles on distilled generators and that training-free teacher-guided endpoint interpolation with adaptive supervision improves motion quality while preserving speed. The trajectory-restoration framing and expanded supporting experiments retain the central claims and contributions.

C2.justification: v1's limitations paragraph focuses on missing inference-time quality checking. v2 adds substantive limitations concerning underrepresented object-motion combinations, source-target structural mismatch, and fine-grained latent attention, linked to the human-to-monkey climbing failure (Appendix D). It also adds interpretations of runtime/memory tradeoffs and discusses unpaired teachers with unshared latent spaces.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly specifies DDIM inversion steps, extraction timestep and attention blocks, guidance schedules, resolutions/frame counts, and VB LoRA, scheduler, and optimization details. Some earlier baseline-initialization and AnimateDiff threshold details disappear. Reproducibility remains limited by Nmax being described as a per-sample event cap while Algorithm 1 caps inner denoising steps. The project link and promised code release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands from the earlier emphasis on UNet diffusion and motion customization to DiT generators, trajectory distribution distillation, and additional guidance approaches. Newly discussed works include Wan, CogVideoX, Video-Blade, DiTFlow, MOFT, OPAD, and FlexiMMT, broadening the research context beyond citation renumbering.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, and method explanation, incorporates Preliminaries within Methods, and reorganizes the appendices around implementation, results, derivation, limitations, and ethics. AnimateDiff discussion moves to the appendix. The narrative restructuring extends beyond simply inserting new experiments.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the pipeline and diagnostic figures, adds runtime bars and DiT/failure panels, restructures tables with backbone and component columns, merges guidance-strength tables, and relocates the AnimateBench table. It also changes typography and page layout and resizes or relocates many retained qualitative figures.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the framework's broad applicability through DiT adaptations and comparisons, broader editing tests, teacher controls, sensitivity/resource analyses, and explicit failure boundaries. Detailed implementation recipes address much of v1's sparse reproducibility documentation. These gains outweigh the loss of noise-initialization ablations and remaining inconsistencies between endpoint formulas, pseudocode, and teacher-budget descriptions, although those inconsistencies still impede exact reproduction.
